headline: Showers Tuesday, then steadier rain Tuesday night and the season's first widespread Cascade snow Wednesday, with a Winter Weather Advisory in effect.
summary: As of Monday evening, showers will come and go across western Washington through Tuesday, with highs in the mid to upper 50s. Another system drops south from British Columbia from Tuesday evening through Wednesday, bringing steadier lowland rain, especially Tuesday night. Southwest winds pick up late Tuesday in parts of southern and central Puget Sound, peaking at 20 to 30 mph from Seattle to Tacoma and west toward Shelton. Forecasters say the biggest impact is the first widespread mountain snow of the season in the Cascades and Olympics. Snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) start around 4,000 to 4,500 feet and fall to 3,000 to 3,500 feet by Wednesday morning, so higher Cascade passes get snow. White Pass and Paradise are forecast to get the most, 6 to 12 inches, locally up to 15 around Paradise. Stevens and Rainy Pass could see 4 to 8 inches, and Snoqualmie Pass up to 3 inches because snow levels there are slightly higher. A Winter Weather Advisory covers the Cascades from 5 PM Tuesday to 5 PM Wednesday, and travelers should check WSDOT for updates. Wednesday highs will be in the low to mid 50s. An upper-level low (a pocket of cold air high in the atmosphere) then lingers over western Washington through at least Friday, keeping showers going, with light snow possible at times in the Cascades and Olympics Thursday and Friday. A slow drying and cooling trend is expected over the weekend into early next week, with a possible frost or freeze threat that forecasters are still watching. They are fairly confident about the Tuesday night to Wednesday system and the low staying through Friday, but less sure how quickly the pattern leaves next weekend, so the timing of drying and frost is uncertain. A Small Craft Advisory covers the offshore coastal waters from Cape Flattery to Cape Shoalwater from 5 AM Tuesday to 5 AM Wednesday.
changes: Early forecasts called for 4 to 6 inches of snow at the passes and a slight lowland thunderstorm chance Wednesday, with no hazards. By afternoon, a Winter Weather Advisory was issued, snow levels were given as starting higher, and the evening update gave pass-by-pass snow totals (up to 3 inches at Snoqualmie) and dropped the thunderstorm mention.
